title: Microbial Physiology, Nutrition, Growth and Reproduction
shortDescription: What microbes need, how they multiply and which factors control their growth in food.
genZNote: Control the growth levers — temperature, pH, water, oxygen — and you control the microbe. Basically parental controls for bacteria.

sections.heading: Nutrition and Physiology
bullets: Requirements: carbon, nitrogen, energy, minerals, vitamins, water. Types: autotroph/heterotroph; phototroph/chemotroph.
Oxygen classes: obligate aerobes (Pseudomonas, Bacillus, moulds), obligate anaerobes (Clostridium), facultative (E. coli, Staphylococcus, yeast), microaerophiles (Campylobacter).

Temperature classes: psychrophile (grow at ≤ 0–5 °C), psychrotroph (grow at refrigeration but optimum higher, e.g. Listeria, Pseudomonas), mesophile (20–45 °C; most pathogens), thermophile (45–80 °C).
Energy production by respiration or fermentation; homofermentative LAB yield mostly lactic acid, heterofermentative produce lactic acid, CO2 and ethanol/acetate.

sections.heading: Growth and Reproduction
bullets: Bacteria reproduce by binary fission; generation time may be ~20 min (E. coli) under ideal conditions; yeasts bud; moulds produce spores; viruses replicate inside host.
Growth curve: lag (adaptation), log/exponential (maximum rate), stationary (nutrient limitation, toxin production), decline/death.
Growth in food: N = N0·2^n (n = generations).
Spores germinate when heat-activated and conditions suit; vegetative cells are destroyed by pasteurization.

sections.heading: Intrinsic and Extrinsic Factors
sections.body: Cardinal temperatures (minimum, optimum, maximum) differ by species. Most spoilage and pathogenic bacteria grow best at neutral pH and aw > 0.95; this explains the importance of refrigeration, acidification and drying.

table.caption: Controlling growth (hurdles)
rows: pH, water activity, nutrients, redox potential, natural antimicrobials (lysozyme, lactoperoxidase), biological structure
Storage temperature, relative humidity, gas atmosphere
Heat, preservatives, packaging, competition among microbes

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Microbial growth in food depends on nutrients, oxygen, temperature, pH and water activity, following a lag–log–stationary–decline pattern, and is controlled by manipulating these factors.
keyFacts: Binary fission; lag, log, stationary, decline.
Facultative anaerobes grow with or without oxygen.

commonTraps: Do not say refrigeration stops all growth — psychrotrophs grow.
